summary: Verified the google_fit retirement change end-to-end (backend + web preview). Backend: 5/5 pytest cases pass in /app/backend/tests/test_iter103_no_google_fit.py — GET /api/connections (logged in as demo@roujaune.app/demo9900) returns exactly the providers [apple_health, health_connect], both kind=device_native / requires_native_build=true / connection_status=requires_build / connected=false; NO provider with id 'google_fit' or name 'Google Fit' is returned, encryption_ready=true, imported_activities=2. Frontend (/connections @ 1280x900 landscape, after email login): the screen renders without any red/error screen, no 'Google Fit' CARD/section is present, and there is exactly one on-page mention of the string 'Google Fit' — descriptive prose inside the HEALTH SYNC blurb ('… Health Connect (Android — covers Samsung Health & Google Fit)'), which explains that Health Connect subsumes Google Fit on-device (not a Google Fit provider card). The 'Available in an installed iOS/Android build with your permission.' note is present exactly once, on the single HEALTH SYNC card (testID health-provider). BLE regression on /connections passed: tapping device-btn-trainer opens ble-panel, ble-scan surfaces all three demo devices (ble-connect-demo-trainer / ble-connect-demo-hr / ble-connect-demo-cadence), and the imported-rides card renders with the 2 seeded outdoor rides. DISCREPANCY vs review request: the frontend does NOT expose testIDs 'provider-apple_health' or 'provider-health_connect' — device-native providers are surfaced via the unified HealthSyncCard (testID='health-provider') because /app/frontend/app/connections.tsx filters `p.kind !== 'device_native'` out of ProviderRow (line 186). This is pre-existing behaviour (no frontend code changed this round, per the agent-to-agent note) and is functionally correct: the two native cards are represented by a single platform-aware HEALTH SYNC card in web preview. Flagging so the main agent can confirm expected UX / testID contract.

integration_issues.issue: Review request expected testIDs 'provider-apple_health' and 'provider-health_connect' but neither is rendered on /connections. Native providers are filtered out of ProviderRow (connections.tsx:186) and represented by the unified HealthSyncCard (testID='health-provider'). No crash, and the required note text is shown. If per-provider testIDs are required, HealthSyncCard needs to render two testID'd cards.

action_items: Optional: if the app spec demands per-provider testIDs 'provider-apple_health' & 'provider-health_connect' on the Connections screen (as stated in the review request), update HealthSyncCard.tsx to render two testID'd rows keyed off /api/connections instead of the single 'health-provider' card. Otherwise no action — the google_fit retirement is complete and the screen is correct.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/providers/__init__.py cleanly documents why google_fit was retired and re-exports registry — good.
backend/routes/connections.py:41 correctly maps native providers (requires_native_build) to connection_status='requires_build' when unlinked — matches frontend HealthSyncCard's 'available' check.

frontend/app/connections.tsx:37 startConnect Alert copy still mentions 'Google Cloud Console' + 'Fitness API' as generic OAuth setup guidance — harmless (only shown when a cloud OAuth provider returns setup_required, and with google_fit removed there is currently no cloud provider surfaced). Consider trimming Google-specific wording since no Google Fit OAuth flow exists anymore.
The HEALTH SYNC card blurb mentions 'Samsung Health & Google Fit' as a descriptor of what Health Connect wraps — this is intentional and NOT a Google Fit provider card. Leave as-is.

success_rate.frontend: 100% for stated google_fit retirement + BLE regression; 1 discrepancy flagged on native-provider testID naming

seed_data_creation: None. Used demo@roujaune.app / demo9900 as per test_credentials.md.
